Lessons.Title: Interpret Representations of Multiplicative Comparison
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will represent situations and descriptions of multiplicative comparison using diagrams and equations.
In this lesson, you analyze and interpret images of discrete objects (connecting cubes) and discrete tape diagrams in which each unit is visible. These diagrams are precursors for more abstract tape diagrams that are used in future lessons. You also make connections between the multiplicative comparison language and multiplication equations.
Core relationship: Connect multiplicative comparison diagrams and equations. Match each tape diagram's number of equal groups to the multiplier.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  How Many Do You See: Times as Many	 (10 minutes); Activity 1: Represent “Times as Many”	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Diagrams to Solve Multiplicative Comparison Problems	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  Comparing Cubes	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: Kiran has 5 cubes and Jada has 4 times as many. How many does Jada have?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): What equation represents 5 equal groups of 3 cubes?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Confusing the number in each group with the number of groups.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Match each tape diagram's number of equal groups to the multiplier.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using addition when a diagram has repeated equal groups.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The mathematical operation or unit interpretation is incorrect.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Three copies of eight represent 3×8, not 3+8.
